plain_english_policy: This bill changes how pesticide companies in Alabama pay to register their products. It switches the registration cycle from every year (annually) to every two years (biennially). To make up for collecting fees less often, it raises the cost per product: new registrations and renewals after 2013 will cost $400 instead of $200. The bill also sets a temporary rule where some companies pay $400 immediately while others pay $200 until their two-year cycle begins in late 2012.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Enactment would increase the financial burden on pesticide registrants by doubling the per-product fee for most renewals starting after December 31, 2012. It simplifies administrative work for the state agency (Board of Agriculture and Industries) by reducing the frequency of renewal processing from annual to biennial cycles.
sponsorship_supports_position: The sponsors support shifting pesticide regulation fees to a two-year cycle with higher per-product costs.
evidence_quotes: to provide that registration of pesticides and pesticide devices shall be biennially; and to provide for the implementation of the new fee schedule.

Upon expiration of registration on December 31, 2011, a registrant whose name begins letters A through M may renew a registration for a period of two years upon payment of a fee of four hundred dollars ($400) per product.
After December 31, 2012, the registrant may renew a registration for a period of two years upon payment of a fee of four hundred dollars ($400) per product.
